# Devil
[color=#ac3a0d]A devilish trickster with a silver tongue making deals around the station.[/color]
A devil is a crew member whose body has been taken over by something from a far worse place. It does not fight. It trades: power, health and second chances, paid for in souls.
Despite their usually not-so-good intentions, a Devil is still considered crew! As a Devil, [color=red][bold]you should not interfere with station affairs unless you are directly asked, or you can make a deal out of it.[/bold][/color]
Under normal circumstances, [color=red][bold]a crew member making a deal with the Devil should be considered a crime.[/bold][/color]
## Spotting a devil - A devil looks like any other crew member and keeps their usual name and job. It is never command, security, the chaplain, the mime, an intern or a borg. - Once a devil holds 2 souls, examining it shows that [italic]their eyes glow a faint red[/italic]. Sunglasses, masks and helmets hide this, and a devil starts with sunglasses. - People who sold their soul have [italic]hollow and soulless[/italic] eyes when examined. - Summoning a contract is loud: the devil's hand bursts into flames with a fireball sound. - A devil cannot throw a punch or fire a gun. [bold]Not everyone with a tail or horns is a devil, that's just specist![/bold]
# Playing a devil
## What you start with - Your [bold]true name[/bold] is in your briefing and in your character menu. Anyone who says it out loud near you hurts you, so keep it secret. - Your backpack holds a [bold]Codex Umbra[/bold] (use it in hand to open the clause list), a [bold]devilish pen[/bold] and sunglasses. - [bold]You cannot fight.[/bold] You have no combat mode, so no melee and no guns. Deals are your only weapon. - You never eat, drink, breathe or feel the temperature or pressure. You cannot become a zombie. Crematoriums, chasms and the supermatter do not touch you. - You take half damage from brute, heat, cold, poison, radiation and bleeding, but [color=red]half again more from holy damage[/color].
## Objectives - [bold]Collect Souls[/bold]: gain 7 to 9 souls. - [bold]Make profitable deals[/bold]: add up 150 to 200 contract weight over the round. Every contract you complete adds its weight. Handshakes and revival contracts add none. - The exact targets are not shown to you, so aim high.
## Your abilities - [bold]Summon infernal contract[/bold] (10 s cooldown): a blank contract appears in your hand. Only you can complete it. - [bold]Shadow jaunt[/bold] (40 s cooldown): turn invisible for 4 seconds and pass through walls. It works while cuffed or downed, and it breaks handcuffs. - [bold]Devils Grip[/bold] (20 s cooldown): puts a burning grip in your hand. Click someone within reach and they are knocked down for 5 seconds, lose 80 stamina, and speak in gibberish for 10 seconds. Anyone holding a bible, or wearing one on their belt, is immune, and the grip is wasted on them. Use the action again to put the grip away. - [bold]Cheat Death[/bold] (250 s cooldown): fully heal, alive or dead, as often as you like. It also breaks handcuffs and resets your other cooldowns. It fails while you carry 100 or more holy damage. - [bold]Summon revival contract[/bold] (2 souls, 30 s cooldown): see below. - [bold]Possess target[/bold] (4 souls, 70 s cooldown): see below.
## Making a deal, step by step 1. Use [bold]Summon infernal contract[/bold]. The contract already reads as follows, which weighs exactly 0:
[color=#999999]Contractee: Soul Ownership Contractee: Death[/color]
2. Click the contract with a pen to edit it. Each clause is its own line, written as [bold]Contractee: Clause[/bold] (the person signing) or [bold]Contractor: Clause[/bold] (you). Use the clause names from the [textlink="clause list" link="DevilClauses"]. 3. Examine the contract up close to see its [bold]weight[/bold]. It must be [bold]0 or more[/bold] to be signed. 4. Give it to your mark. They hold any pen in their active hand and alt-click the contract (or use the [bold]Sign[/bold] verb). They sign first. 5. Countersign it the same way. Every clause takes effect the moment you sign, and if it holds [bold]Soul Ownership[/bold] for the contractee, you gain their soul.
The clause lines are strict: - The line must start with the prefix and hold nothing else. Bullets, bold text, a trailing full stop or a hyphen break it. - Capitals and spaces in the clause name do not matter, so "Fear of Fire", "fear of fire" and "FearOfFire" all work. - Any line that is not a clause is ignored, so you can write as much fine print around them as you like. - Each clause counts once, whichever side it is on. Writing it twice only applies the first copy.
## Contract weight Each clause has a weight. [bold]Negative weight is good for whoever gets the clause, and positive weight is bad for them.[/bold] Weights add up the same no matter which side a clause is on.
For example, Soul Ownership (+25) and Weakness (-35) add up to -10, so nobody can sign it. Add "Contractee: Voice" (+20) and the total is +10. Now it can be signed, and the signer is muted on top of everything else.
Watch out for two things: - A clause written on [bold]Contractor:[/bold] really does happen to you. "Contractor: Death" or "Contractor: Mortality" even replaces your own unlimited Cheat Death with a weaker one. - Every clause that changes damage taken (Weakness, Strength, Fear of Fire) replaces the target's whole damage profile, including any species resistances, and the last one written wins.
Until both parties have signed, you can [bold]Burn contract[/bold] with its alt verb to destroy it. Careful: alt-clicking a contract with no pen in hand burns it. Contracts cannot be cremated, sold or dropped into chasms, but they can be eaten.
## Souls and power You gain a soul from a completed contract with Soul Ownership, a handshake, or an accepted revival contract. - [bold]2 souls[/bold]: Summon revival contract, and your eyes start to glow. - [bold]4 souls[/bold]: Possess target. - [bold]6 souls[/bold]: your possessions last longer. Nothing else is unlocked.
## Handshakes Right-click someone within reach and pick [bold]Offer handshake[/bold]. They have 15 seconds to right-click you and pick [bold]Shake (name)'s hand[/bold]. If they do, they are fully healed and get one Cheat Death, but you take their soul, and they gain one random harmful clause. The harmful clause can even be Time (death in five minutes). Mindshielded people, silicons and anyone already condemned cannot take your hand.
## Revival contracts Hold a [bold]contract from the depths[/bold] and click a corpse within reach. If the dead player has ghosted, they are asked whether to sell their soul for a second chance. If they accept, the body is fully healed, they return to it, you gain the soul, and the contract is used up. If they refuse, you can offer it again later. This ignores mindshields. The clauses printed on it are only for show.
## Possession Use [bold]Possess target[/bold] on someone within reach who has [bold]sold their soul[/bold]. Nobody else can be possessed. You control their body for 60 seconds, or 90 at 6 souls. Your own body turns invisible meanwhile, and you can return early with [bold]End possession[/bold]. You cannot hurt anyone in a possessed body. When it ends, you reappear beside the host, and they are paralyzed for 10 seconds. Mindshields do not stop possession, but chaplains cannot be possessed.
# Facing a devil
## Selling your soul - You become [bold]condemned[/bold]. You can never make another deal or shake a devil's hand, and the devil can possess you whenever it is nearby. - Holy things now hurt you too. - The default contract gives you one Cheat Death. If you die with no Cheat Death left, you are [bold][color=red]dragged to hell[/color][/bold]: the body is gone, and nobody can revive you. - Some souls are already spoken for. The chaplain, the lawyer and the captain cannot sign contracts, take a handshake, be revived by contract or be possessed. Neither can silicons or anyone with a mindshield, though a revival contract still works on a mindshielded corpse.
## Hurting a devil - [bold]Its true name.[/bold] It is not on the devil's ID or its contracts, which are signed with its everyday name, so you have to get it out of the devil. Say it aloud within earshot: the devil takes 15 holy damage and is paralyzed for 4 seconds. This works at most once every 30 seconds. Silicons and people without their own soul (the condemned, the chaplain, the lawyer and the captain) have no power over the name. A chaplain from Central Command doubles the effect. - [bold]A chaplain's bible[/bold] sears a devil for 50 holy damage and paralyzes it for 16 seconds. - [bold]Holy water[/bold] and [bold]holy weapons[/bold] such as the chaplain's swords also deal holy damage. - Carry a bible in your hand or on your belt to shrug off the Devils Grip.
## Getting rid of one A devil's body can be killed, but it cannot be gibbed, and it can Cheat Death again and again. [bold]Keep its holy damage at 100 or more[/bold] and it cannot revive. Holy damage slowly wears off by itself, so keep it topped up.
To banish it, the chaplain uses their bible on the devil while it is critical or dead. This is a 10-second exorcism, broken if the chaplain moves or drops the bible. The devil is then cast out for [bold]3 minutes[/bold], and returns with a completely new face, name, DNA and fingerprints.
## Trickery goes both ways! Weight counts the same whichever side a clause is on. If you can talk a devil into signing a clause that harms the [italic]Contractor[/italic], you can take good clauses for free.
